entries.path: data/lunge/Patellofemoral Joint Loading in Forward Lunge With Step Length and Height Variations.pdf
entries.reason: Escamilla 2022 (J Appl Biomech; not the IJSPT forward/side lunge paper already in front_knee_too_deep/): a short step makes the lead knee travel past the toes from about 60 degrees of knee flexion and gives higher patellofemoral force/stress at deep knee angles; authors say knee translation past the toes may be harmful and should be avoided. Matches the excessive_front_knee_flexion card ('a step that is too short ... forces the front knee to fold sharply'; extra knee load). Caution: its PFPS rehab progression starts with 'mini' lunges (0-40 degrees) - rehab context, ends at full depth, but the curator could tag it shallow_lunge.

entries.path: data/lunge/Influence of Different Load Conditions on Lower Extremity Biomechanics during the Lunge Squat in Novice Men.pdf
entries.reason: Gao 2022 (Bioengineering): forward lunge in 14 novice men with dumbbell, barbell and weighted vest at 25% and 50% BW (OpenSim joint angles, moments, COP). Load type is not a rule, and most form content is already in the curated Gao 2025 paper from the same group (novices lean forward -> knee shear; Farrokhi trunk lean -> more hip extensor work; dumbbells for beginners). New to the KB: one discussion sentence that small knee flexion points to quadriceps weakness and limited ankle dorsiflexion (cited) - the only shallow_lunge cause found so far; the KB has no shallow_lunge cause item. Cautions: it cites Escamilla as advising caution with a LONG-step lunge to reduce patellar force (the curated Escamilla papers say the short step is the problem) - opposite of the excessive_front_knee_flexion card; equipment advice (vest for knee pain) is off-rule; trunk upright / knee behind toes / rear knee near the floor are protocol. Four pages carry a duplicate 'FOR PEER REVIEW' text layer, so some windows repeat text. Unsure - kept.
entries.read: full text (abstract, introduction, methods, discussion, conclusion) + compared with the curated Gao 2025 paper + shallow_lunge items in curated_data_v6

entries.reason: Helme 2020 (JSCR accepted manuscript): rear foot elevated split squat 5RM, two force plates - the lead foot gives about 84% of vertical force and the rear foot only about the leg's own mass, so the authors class the RFESS as unilateral. Nothing on faults, causes or fixes. Form appears only as the technique protocol (front heel down, neutral posture, rear hip about 180 degrees, rear knee down to lead-ankle height) and a note that depth was not standardised. Bar displacement fell slightly as load rose, but every rep met the depth minimum, so it does not describe shallow lunging. The rear-leg content is force share, not the bent/straight rear knee behind straight_back_leg; rear-leg forces are already covered by the curated Arakawa 2025 and Jaeggi 2024.

entries.path: data/lunge/Biomechanical Analysis of the Anterior Lunge During 4 External-Load Conditions.pdf
entries.reason: Riemann 2012 (J Athl Train): anterior lunge at 0/12.5/25/50% body mass, joint angles, moment impulse and work. Mostly hip-vs-knee-vs-ankle kinetics, which is not a rule. One usable passage for shallow_lunge: under the 50% load participants did not lower as far (centre of mass 2 cm higher), and the authors advise practitioners to monitor lunge depth and cue clients under heavier loads so they work through the full range of motion - a cause (heavy load) plus a fix (depth cue). Caveat: peak knee flexion did not change significantly (96 -> 92 degrees of flexion, about 84-88 degrees interior), so no condition was a shallow lunge by the rule's 105-degree bar. Trunk content (flexed trunk shifts load to hip and ankle, upright trunk to the knee) is cited from Farrokhi, already in the KB; erect torso and step length are protocol. Nothing on the rear knee.

entries.path: data/lunge/Common Mistakes to Avoid When Performing a Lunge in Ladera Ranch.pdf
entries.reason: Local fitness-business web article (no author, no references, keyword-stuffed with 'lunge in Ladera Ranch'), 3 pages, about one window. Mistake list: knee far past the toes stresses the knee (excessive_front_knee_flexion oq1, but not tied to over-bending), a step that is too short forces the knee forward (oq2), forward torso lean shifts work off the legs and strains the lower back with an upright-chest fix (forward_trunk_lean mistake + consequence + fix, already well covered), core bracing, pushing off the back leg, rushing, looking down, warm-up, tightrope foot placement (not rules). 'Step far enough that both knees form about 90 degrees at the bottom' is a principle for shallow_lunge and straight_back_leg, both already past the principle threshold. No shallow-lunge or straight-rear-leg mistake or consequence. Unsure - kept because it is cheap.

entries.path: data/lunge/Hip-Muscle Activation during the Lunge, Single-Leg Squat, and Step-Up-and-Over Exercises.pdf
entries.reason: Boudreau 2009 (J Sport Rehabil): hip-muscle EMG across step-up-and-over, lunge and single-leg squat to build a rehab progression (SUO -> lunge -> SLSQ). Lunge form is protocol only (step 100% of leg length). The one depth sentence is about the single-leg squat (60 vs 90 degrees) explaining EMG differences from other studies. No faults, causes, consequences or fixes.

entries.path: data/lunge/IMPROVED MUSCLE ACTIVATION IN PERFORMING A BODY WEIGHT LUNGE COMPARED TO THE TRADITIONAL BACK SQUAT.pdf
entries.reason: Dwelly et al. (4-page conference paper, n = 8 female athletes): EMG of bodyweight lunge vs back squat to 90/60/30 degrees of knee flexion. The lunge is a single condition with no depth or form variation; lunge form is only 'knees flexed to 90 degrees'. The squat-depth result (90-degree squat activates quadriceps and hamstrings more than 60/30) is partial_squat consequence, but in the lunge folder those windows would be cut as folder mismatch, and partial_squat already passes. Muscle activity only.

entries.path: data/push-up/COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF ELBOW JOINT LOADING IN PUSH-UP AND BENCH-PRESS.pdf
entries.reason: Chou 2011 (Biomed Eng Appl Basis Commun): elbow joint forces and EMG, push-up vs bench press. Peak elbow flexion 93 degrees in both (protocol). The authors explain that peak elbow force occurs between 90 degrees and the bottom, and conclude that bench press gives more activation with less elbow load - as push-up items this reads as 'going deep loads the elbow' and would contradict partial_pushup (the u082 pattern). Nothing on body line.

entries.path: data/push-up/Force transmission through the wrist during performance of push-ups on a hyperextended and a neutral wrist.pdf
entries.reason: Polovinets 2017 (J Hand Ther): ground reaction force direction through the wrist in push-ups on a hyperextended wrist vs a neutral (fist) wrist, n = 14. Wrist/hand position is excluded by both push-up cards (hand placement). No depth or body-line content; injury mentions are wrist, shoulder and elbow loading.

entries.path: data/push-up/Optimal activation ratio of the scapular muscles in closed kinetic chain shoulder exercises A systematic review.pdf
entries.reason: Mendez-Rebolledo 2021 (J Back Musculoskelet Rehabil) systematic review: upper trapezius vs lower/middle trapezius and serratus anterior EMG ratios across push-up, push-up plus, plank, pull-up variants. Scapular muscles are excluded by the push-up cards. Trap: its 'Half Push Up' is an incline push-up (trunk at 45 degrees, hands on a 30 cm box), not a partial-range push-up, and the review rates it 'optimal' - if curated it could be tagged partial_pushup and read as recommending half push-ups. Knee push-ups appear only as EMG variants, not as regressions for a fault.

BOXROX summary of Mike Israetel (Renaissance Periodization) on walking-lunge mistakes. 'Cutting depth' (not going all the way down) is named the most common mistake, with a consequence (muscles grow more when stretched through a long range, more motor units recruited) and a fix (go down until the knee touches or nearly touches the ground, under control) - shallow_lunge mistake + consequence + fix, the consequence slot the KB lacks. Also: steps too short cause knee discomfort (excessive_front_knee_flexion oq2), tilting forward at the bottom shifts work to back and hamstrings, fix upright and braced (forward_trunk_lean). Grip, load choice, resetting between steps are off-rule. Magazine retelling of a coach's video. Not fetchable by the curator as is: trafilatura.fetch_url gets a page with no extractable article (site needs a browser User-Agent; fetched with one: 6285 chars).

entries.reason: ClassPass blog quoting two personal trainers (one NASM master trainer). Usable: stepping too far back means no proper 90-degree bend and the back knee absorbs the pressure (straight_back_leg cause, step too long); too much forward bending of the upper body (forward_trunk_lean); front knee past the ankle (oq1); proper form = lower the back knee until both knees are about 90 degrees. CONFLICT: it suggests 'a forward lunge without the back leg bending' as an easier regression, which contradicts straight_back_leg - after curating, find that item and untag or delete it. Bad-knee/bad-ankle advice, traveling lunges, tempo schemes, and a quote of the Dwelly EMG study are off-rule. Unsure - kept.

Experience Life (Life Time) list of split-squat and lunge errors. 'Stance too long': the back knee does not bend as much, which puts a lot of pressure on it and over time causes knee pain - straight_back_leg cause (step too long, listed on the card) + consequence, the first mistake/consequence source for that rule. Fix: set up from half-kneeling to find a stance that lets both knees bend to about 90 degrees pain-free. Also tightrope stance and too much weight on the back foot (off-rule). The card's consequence is load shifting to the front knee; this one is load on the back knee, still a consequence of the rear knee not bending. Short (about 1,800 chars, one window).

entries.reason: Attika Fitness (gym blog), 5 push-up mistakes. partial_pushup: 'half reps = half results', bending the elbows only a little and stopping far above the ground means the chest isn't working to its potential; fix = fewer reps, focus on depth, hands on a box or bench; principle = chest nearly touches the floor (mistake + consequence + fix + principle). hip_sag_or_pike: hips lifting (pike) from a disengaged core, hips sagging from a tired core putting pressure on the lower back; fix = brace, plank basics, knee push-ups. Elbow flare and shoulder shrugging are off-rule.

ATHLEAN-X, Jeff Cavaliere (MSPT, CSCS). Whole article is partial_pushup: chasing rep counts and speed shortens the range by an inch or two at the bottom (cause + mistake), which significantly reduces the effectiveness and limits the work of the upper body (consequence); fix = chest touches the floor without disengaging, slow cadence, end the set when rep speed drops; strict reps cut the count by about 60%. Caveats: the top-lockout half of the advice is excluded by the card (rule only checks the bottom); pull-up and squat analogies; program-marketing text at the end.

Cathe Friedman blog, 6 push-up mistakes. partial_pushup: 'short range' push-ups with only partly bent elbows are cheating and greatly reduce the benefits; go down to an elbow angle of 90 degrees or less, chest to the floor if comfortable; if you cannot, use knee or hands-elevated push-ups (mistake + consequence + fix + principle). hip_sag_or_pike: back and hips sag from a weak core; fix = planks; straight line from feet to head. Caveat: the speed section suggests 'going half-way down and holding' as an isometric variation - that item may read as endorsing half reps; untag after curating. Hand position, neck, variations are off-rule.

Fitness and Power long form guide (no author). hip_sag_or_pike: sagging hips are the most common fault, caused by a weak core and insufficient quad activation; reduce core work, shorten the range and load the lumbar spine; five-point alignment. partial_pushup: partial range is ego- or fatigue-driven; fix = fewer full reps, stop the set when depth is lost; upper chest to within millimetres of the floor. Caveats, several against the cards or other sources: 'err toward hips higher, piking is relatively safe' (the rule flags both); 'contract the quads, not the glutes' (card fix says squeeze the glutes); it calls feet-elevated push-ups 'incline' (the card's incline regression is hands elevated) so a beginner could be pointed to the harder variation; elbows at 10-20 degrees is an outlier claim. Unsure - kept. Not fetchable by the curator as is: trafilatura.fetch_url gets a page with no extractable article (site needs a browser User-Agent; fetched with one: 12981 chars).

elitefts article (Brian LeRiche, NSCA CSCS, 2019). The live URL now redirects to a 404 (both the old /blogs/motivation/ address and /education/); text read in full from the Wayback Machine capture of 2020-10-30.
